author: kevaundray
content:
> that could also give it extra reorg power, which may be dangerous and have unintended implications

If every node says at "slot N this block is final/canonical", and we wont reorg it. Then the issue I can see is that if we choose a bad set of validators for that slot, then they could cause a reorg. Is this the issue you were thinking of?

> im also not sure about keeping BLS slashings post PQ fork, because if BLS is broken by then, honest validators can get slashed by forged BLS attestations. that seems worse

I agree, though I think its fine to assume this in the happy path

author: kevaundray
content:
> I think in all cases, non-PQ validators should keep the normal withdrawal delay at the transition. i don’t see a reason not to do this, it deters bad behavior close to the fork

One corner case here is that the non-PQ validators will still be selected for duties until `exit_epoch` but without PQ credentials, they would essentially be seen as inactive I think

author: kevaundray
content: I guess its probably fine, given we would only switch over to the PQ fork when 66% or more of validators have registered their PQ credentials
